content: The medications you take may either work effectively or increase your risk of experiencing serious side effects. This document does not include all potential drug interactions. It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Mesalamine is closely related to other medications such as balsalazide, olsalazine, and sulfasalazine. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine normetanephrine levels, potentially leading to inaccurate test results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Before starting this medication and during its use, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as liver and kidney function tests, to monitor your health. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. If the medication bottle contains a desiccant, keep it in the bottle. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. When taking mesalamine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminosalicylates (e.g., balsalazide, olsalazine), salicylates (e.g., aspirin, salsalate), or sulfasalazine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight, especially if you have skin conditions such as atopic dermatitis or eczema. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Mesalamine is similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 years old should not take aspirin or aspirin-related medications (e.g., salicylates) if they have chickenpox, the flu, an undiagnosed illness, or have recently received a vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If you experience side effects such as stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, constipation, headache, or joint/muscle pain, these may occur. Occasionally, you may notice whole or partial tablets/capsules in your stool. If this happens frequently, inform your doctor. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, mesalamine may worsen ulcerative colitis or cause a severe allergic reaction. For side effects, U.S. residents should contact their doctor for medical advice, and Canadian residents should do the same. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most current and complete information about this medication and your health needs.
